# Shared Proxy

One Nginx can serve several ɳSelf projects on a host. The project that owns the Nginx sets `NGINX_MODE=shared`. Each other project is nested in a sub-directory of the owner and sets `NGINX_FRONTED_BY=<owner directory name>`. This page covers what `nself build` does for each side. Starting, attaching networks and reloading Nginx belong to `nself start` and are not described here.

Without `NGINX_MODE=shared` on the owner nothing changes: a fronted project still writes plain, unprefixed site files into the owner's `nginx/sites`, exactly as before.

---

## Layout

```
stack/                    owner: NGINX_MODE=shared
  nginx/sites/            site confs of every project
  nginx/shared/           registrations (written by nself build)
  ssl/certificates/       certificate pairs of every project
  backend/                fronted project: NGINX_FRONTED_BY=stack
```

The fronted project must live directly under a directory named after `NGINX_FRONTED_BY`. Any other layout is refused, as before.

A fronted project named `backend` inside the owner directory makes `nself build` run in the owner directory treat the owner as a monorepo and build `backend` instead ("Detected monorepo layout"). Build the owner with `nself build --no-monorepo`, or give the fronted project another directory name.

## What the owner's build does

- Creates `nginx/shared/` and writes `_owner.json` (service names, server names, upstream hosts that stay as written).
- Writes its own routes with container names as upstreams: `<PROJECT_NAME>_hasura:8080`, not `hasura:8080`. A bare service name is ambiguous once one Nginx reaches two projects, because every project has a `hasura`. Container names are unique per host.
- Leaves plugin and hand-managed upstreams as written.
- Never deletes a file that a registration lists.
- Warns about each registration whose project directory is gone, and prints how to remove it.

## What a fronted project's build does

When the owner has `nginx/shared/` with a `_owner.json` (the owner's build writes it; a `nginx/shared/` without it means the owner dropped shared mode, and the project's files are then removed, see Leaving):

- Writes container-name upstreams for its own services (core, optional, custom, installed plugins). Frontend routes point at `host.docker.internal`, which is not a service, so they stay as written. A plugin upstream is rewritten when its host is a service of this project (plugin containers are `<PROJECT_NAME>_<name>`).
- Names its site files `<PROJECT_NAME>.<file>` (`bproj.hasura.conf`) and stamps them `# Generated by nself build (project bproj)`.
- Copies each certificate pair its confs reference into the owner's `ssl/certificates/<dir>` (directory mode 0700, key 0600).
- Writes `nginx/shared/<PROJECT_NAME>.json` listing every file it put under the owner.
- Removes only files its own previous registration listed and the new one does not.

### Certificates

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Directory does not exist in the owner's `ssl/` | Pair is copied |
| Directory is listed in this project's registration | Replaced on rotation (temp directory, then rename) |
| Own directory already holds a certificate that expires later | Kept (an ACME renewal installed it) |
| Identical pair held by someone else | Reused, not listed |
| Different pair not owned by this project | `E503` |
| Directory managed by ACME (symlink to a generation directory, recorded in `ssl/.acme/lineages.json`) | Left alone, never listed, never removed |
| Any other symlink on the path, or no write permission | `E503`, nothing written |
| This project has no local pair yet (first build, or `ssl/` cleaned) and the directory exists in the owner's `ssl/` | Own directory: kept and stays listed. Anyone else's: `E503` (it cannot be proven identical) |

## Refusals

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `E503` | A project name that equals one of its own conf stems (`PROJECT_NAME=hasura`); a server name or certificate directory is already served by the owner or another registered project; a registration does not validate; the owner's `ssl/` cannot be written safely |
| `E504` | An upstream host that stays as written (a single label, such as `sidecar`) is a service name or upstream host of the owner or another registered project |
| `E505` | `NGINX_MODE` is not `shared`; `NGINX_MODE=shared` together with `NGINX_FRONTED_BY`; `NGINX_MODE=shared` with a proxy provider other than nginx |

The checks run before any file is written, so a refused build changes nothing. `E505` for an unknown mode or for `shared` with `NGINX_FRONTED_BY` is a warning in v1.4 and an error from v1.5. `NGINX_MODE=shared` with the traefik provider is an error in both.

Host names with a dot, IP addresses and `localhost` resolve the same for every project and are never refused by `E504`.

## Leaving

Unsetting `NGINX_FRONTED_BY` in the fronted project, or the owner unsetting `NGINX_MODE`, makes the next build of the fronted project remove every file its registration lists, then the registration. Files in an ACME-managed directory are not touched.

## Registration file

`nginx/shared/<project>.json`, generated, schema `schemas/shared-proxy.v1.schema.json`:

```json
{
  "_generated": "GENERATED BY nself build - DO NOT HAND EDIT",
  "files": ["nginx/sites/bproj.hasura.conf", "ssl/certificates/b-test/fullchain.pem"],
  "network": "bproj_network",
  "project": "bproj",
  "project_dir": "/srv/stack/backend",
  "schema_version": "1",
  "server_names": ["api.b.test"],
  "service_names": ["auth", "hasura", "postgres"],
  "verbatim_upstream_hosts": []
}
```

The file name must equal `<project>.json`, a project is registered once, and `project_dir` must be under the owner. Keys and lists are sorted.
